title: Two whole human chromosomes of the reference assembly GRCh38.p14, chromosomes 21 and 22, as FASTA from NCBI RefSeq
provider: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), RefSeq, through the E-utilities (efetch)
credit: Chromosomes: NCBI RefSeq, GRCh38.p14 (Genome Reference Consortium)
format: FASTA (one record each, 70 bases a line), the chromosome's bases from its first, numbered as the accession numbers them (the coordinates of HGVS g. descriptions on NC_000021.9 and NC_000022.11, and of ISCN's bands). The short arms, the centromeres and the gaps of the assembly are runs of N (chromosome 22 begins with about 10.5 Mb of them), which the domains treat as unknown bases.
coverage: NC_000021.9 (chromosome 21, 46,709,983 bp) and NC_000022.11 (chromosome 22, 50,818,468 bp), the primary assembly's chromosomes, without alternate loci or patches
licence: NCBI places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the GenBank and RefSeq data (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/); the Genome Reference Consortium's assemblies are public. The files are fetched into the cache and not redistributed.
citation: Schneider, V. A. et al. (2017), Evaluation of GRCh38 and de novo haploid genome assemblies demonstrates the enduring quality of the reference assembly, Genome Research 27, 849-864; O'Leary, N. A. et al. (2016), Reference sequence (RefSeq) database at NCBI: current status, taxonomic expansion, and functional annotation, Nucleic Acids Research 44, D733-D745.
used_by: domains/genomics/structural (structural variants, copy number and aneuploidy simulated on real human chromosomes and called back, described in HGVS and ISCN)
